recipes.purpose: Show a true two-period change when the values cannot be expressed more clearly as one non-negative actual value against a prior or reference benchmark.
recipes.data: Exactly 2 labeled numeric values with measure.quantity, matching scope, and explicit periods. For two positive level values, prefer comparison.benchmark-gap with the later/current value as value and the earlier/reference value as benchmark.
bestFor: native rates or indexes where benchmark-gap level semantics do not apply

recipes.purpose: Compare actual, expected, target, or alternative values of one named quantity for one shared scope and period. Do not flatten repeated category/time pairs into separate scenario bars.
recipes.data: 2 to 5 labeled numeric values with measure.quantity and matching scope and period. A two-item standalone chart also needs a numeric reference, basis, or source-supported mechanism, consequence, denominator, or comparison fact; otherwise enrich, merge, or omit it. Two categories with earlier/later values should use comparison.benchmark-gap; three or more paired categories should use comparison.dumbbell.

recipes.purpose: Compare positive and negative changes in one named quantity for one shared scope and period.
recipes.data: 2 to 10 labeled numeric changes with measure.quantity and matching scope and period; values may be positive or negative.

recipes.purpose: Show exact values, min-max intervals, and thresholds for one named quantity on one scale.
recipes.data: 1 to 8 items with value or low/high fields, measure.quantity, and matching scope and period. A single interval requires a visible benchmark or reference that supplies the total or threshold scale and is invalid when visualEvidenceAudit contains three or more named comparable observations.

recipes.purpose: Show one non-negative actual or current level against a meaningful benchmark so the gap, premium, shortfall, overage, or before-versus-after difference is visible in one compact bar.
recipes.data: 1 to 6 labeled items with an underlying actual/current value and benchmark/reference value in one unit, plus matching quantity and scope. Use one item whenever two positive levels can be read naturally as actual/current versus benchmark/prior. For one or two category-level before/after pairs, encode the later/current level as value and the earlier/prior level as benchmark. Two meaningful policy, target, or payout shares may use separate rows against one shared tangible total when that gives the viewer a stronger anchor than a hypothetical composition.

recipes.purpose: Visualize two source-supported causal drivers converging on a different outcome without forcing them onto a shared axis.
recipes.data: Exactly 3 items: two relationshipRole driver items and one outcome item, all with distinct real-world quantities. relationship.formula must state the source-supported mechanism. Every item needs a value or range, direction, displayValue, quantity, scope, and period. Repeated prices, repeated volumes, and the same measure at different dates must use change, scenarios, dumbbell, or trend geometry. Each item is drawn on its own local quantitative signal; the two driver connectors join directly into one outcome path, and connector width encodes no magnitude.

recipes.purpose: Compare two values for several categories while preserving the direction and size of every category-level change.
recipes.data: 3 to 10 labeled items with value and benchmark in one unit, plus matching quantity, scope, and period. benchmark is the earlier or reference value; value is the later or actual value. Different categories may have different absolute levels; what must remain comparable is each category's own earlier-versus-later pair in the same unit and basis.
bestFor: target versus actual across several categories

recipes.data: At least 3 ordered labeled numeric values; 5 or more preferred.

recipes.purpose: Show dated policy, restriction, outage, contract, or operational intervals on a common calendar.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 labeled intervals with ISO start and end dates, or exact duration plus durationUnit when all intervals share timeline.anchorDate. Tone controls the interval color; displayValue names the duration.

recipes.purpose: Show parts of a whole when the shape of the composition matters.
Show exact parts of one total in a compact horizontal composition when the mix itself is the finding.
recipes.data: 2 to 6 positive labeled numeric values. Do not use a single hypothetical split when the source provides a meaningful policy, target, prior, or alternative share against the same tangible total; in that case prefer shared-total benchmark geometry.

recipes.purpose: Compare exact positive additive components of one reported total with every component seated at zero and the total shown as a numeric reference.
recipes.data: 2 to 6 positive labeled component values with one shared quantity, scope, and period. Exactly one numeric reference must equal the reported total within display precision. Do not include the total as a redundant data row.
bestFor: budget components where component magnitude matters

recipes.purpose: Explain how an existing balance or level moves through exact positive and negative changes into a reported ending amount.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 ordered items with role start, change, subtotal, or end; every item also needs reported valueStatus, period, and scope, and the values must reconcile. Do not use waterfall when the intermediate values are simply positive components of one total; use composition.components so every component starts at zero.
bestFor: balance movements with genuine increases and decreases

recipes.purpose: Rank categories where labels need horizontal space.
Show a geographic breakdown across named continental administrative regions with collision-managed callout cards.
recipes.data: 1 to 12 items with a regionId or regionIds plus status, tone, value, or concise evidence.

composableFeatures.purpose: Add target, average, legal limit, prior norm, or other numeric reference lines without changing recipe.
Attach one short explanatory note to a specific data point or stage.

Use logarithmic scale only for genuinely multiplicative comparisons across orders of magnitude. Never use it when the point is that an amount is a small fraction of a benchmark or denominator; preserve that proportional gap with a linear scale and period-normalize an oversized monthly or annual flow benchmark when needed.
Add up to four genuinely secondary contextual facts after a primary visual that already contains at least two quantitative or geographic marks. Supporting facts cannot be the chart.
Expose the tangible numerator and denominator behind a share or ratio, or the total population and affected count behind a risk estimate.
